headline: Brazil Unemployment Rate Reaches Record Low Of 5.1 Percent In October
seoTitle: Brazil Unemployment Rate Falls to 5.1 Percent
metaDescription: The Brazilian unemployment rate reached 5.1 percent for the period ending in October, matching the lowest level recorded in the IBGE historical series.
aiSummaryBullets: Brazil's unemployment rate fell to 5.1 percent in the three-month period ending in October.
The figure matches the historical low previously recorded in December 2025.
Data published by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics align with market expectations.
aiContextParagraph: The Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE) released labor market data on Friday showing that the national unemployment rate reached 5.1 percent for the quarter concluding in October 2026. This result equals the lowest point in the historical data series, which has been maintained by the agency since 2012. Analysts noted that the latest unemployment figure met market expectations and demonstrated resilience despite indicators of economic deceleration in the country. The report is based on the Continuous National Household Sample Survey, known as Pnad Contínua, which tracks employment trends across the population. While previous lows were reached in December 2025, current indicators suggest the labor market remains at its peak performance level for this interval, reflecting a period of relative stability in employment statistics during the final quarter of the year despite broader economic challenges.
whyItIsViral: The report gained traction through coverage by three independent news outlets following the official release of national economic data.
